purpose: dharma (religious merit) of the commissioner; merit transferred so that all beings attain Sukhāvatī
notes: The catalogue gives the place of copying as Kathmandu. That is where the commissioner lived (yadesa kyalatora = Keltol, Kathmandu). The colophon itself says the copy was written in Lhasa, at Mudariṃgā ('hlāsa mudariṃgāsa coyā jula'), by a Mānandhar scribe from Kirtipur (kipudesa). This fits the Newar merchant communities in Lhasa. 'Jiodhanaṃ' is read as Jīvadhana. 'Cakanāsiṃ' is read as Cakanāsiṃha, though it could also be a Newari personal name such as Cakanā Siṃ. The book is called 'vasudhārādeviyā pustaka' (the book of the goddess Vasudhārā) and was made 'dharmmacesnā svacita' (out of religious intent, by his own wish). This may mean Cakanāsiṃha offered it as well as commissioning it, but the colophon does not say so explicitly, so the role is kept as commissioner only. Dates: Dillā = Āṣāḍha; NS 959 = 1839 CE.
